row.evidence: Okta's catalogue page says the MongoDB Atlas integration "supports SAML-based Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM-based automated user provisioning", but MongoDB's own Atlas docs describe only SAML federation with just-in-time provisioning and role mapping, and no SCIM endpoint or plan.
row.notes: Status unknown: the only SCIM evidence is Okta's OIN listing (updated Sep. 18 2026: SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push, Entitlement Management ticked); the Atlas docs index, sitemap and docs search return no SCIM page, so there is no vendor-documented endpoint or plan gate. Atlas is usage-priced (Free M0, Flex $0.011/hour up to $30/month, Dedicated from $0.08/hour), not per user, so per-user fields stay null. Federated Authentication (SAML) with domain, organization and role mapping is documented with no tier restriction stated; users are created just-in-time on first IdP sign-in (Entra's tutorial says JIT is on by default). The Atlas Administration API v2 manages org and project users, teams, invitations and roles (service-account OAuth 2.0 or legacy digest API keys) and exposes an organization events (activity feed) API.

plans.name: Free (M0)
plans.notes: Admin API is organization-level and not described as tier-limited.

plans.name: Flex
plans.notes: Usage-based: billed hourly with monthly invoices.

roles.how: Not SCIM: Atlas maps IdP groups (memberOf) to organization and project roles at each federated login.

scim.notes: MongoDB's docs do not document a SCIM endpoint; Okta's OIN page claims SCIM-based provisioning (see idp_apps.okta).

auth.notes: Service-account OAuth 2.0 client-credentials tokens (1 hour lifespan) or legacy API key pairs over HTTP Digest; access is limited by Atlas roles assigned to the service account, not scopes.

capabilities.notes: delete_user = remove the user from the organization; teams are the group object.

rate_limits.text: Token-bucket rate limits per endpoint set and scope (organization, project, user or IP); 429 when the bucket is empty.

okta.notes: OIN ticks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Entitlement Management. Okta app key is mongodbcloudmanager; who built the connector is not stated, and MongoDB documents no SCIM endpoint.

entra.notes: Gallery app 'MongoDB Atlas - SSO' supports SP and IdP-initiated SSO and just-in-time user provisioning only.

google.notes: MongoDB documents Google Workspace as a SAML IdP for federated auth; no Google catalogue page checked.

conflicts.text: Okta's OIN page lists SCIM provisioning (Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push) for MongoDB Atlas, while MongoDB's own Atlas docs describe only SAML federation with just-in-time provisioning and Entra's tutorial lists JIT only.

searched: MongoDB docs search API (docs-search-transport.mongodb.com): scim -> no results
open_questions: MongoDB does not document the SCIM connector Okta lists: endpoint, plan, attributes, and whether deactivation removes the user from the organization are unknown.
Who built the Okta SCIM connector (MongoDB or Okta) is not stated on the OIN page.
Atlas docs do not say whether Federated Authentication is limited to any cluster tier or support plan.
No user-event webhooks documented; Atlas alerts/third-party webhooks were not checked for user events.
Google Workspace, OneLogin and JumpCloud catalogue pages were not checked.
